desc:
Product recommendation performance reports show what your suggestions are doing: views, clicks, add to carts and linked revenue. Ecom Swift LLC pulls the data together and writes it up in plain English, with charts and clear next steps.

## Why you need to measure suggestions

Adding a recommendation block feels like progress, but a block that nobody clicks is only clutter. Many stores install a tool, see a few orders tagged to it and assume it works. Others see no tag at all and assume it does nothing.

Neither guess is reliable. A report that separates placements, devices and visitor types tells you which blocks to keep, which to change and which to remove.

## What is a recommendation performance report?

A recommendation performance report is a written summary of how product suggestions behave in your store. It counts how many shoppers saw a block, how many clicked, how many added to cart and how much revenue is linked to those actions. A good report also explains how each number was measured.

## What the numbers help you decide

Reports turn questions into choices. If the cart block has many clicks but few orders, the suggestions may be attractive but poorly priced. If a product page block has few views, it may sit too low on the page. If phone shoppers click far less than desktop shoppers, the layout may need work.

Linked revenue needs careful reading. A shopper might have bought the item anyway, so linked revenue is not the same as extra revenue. We say this plainly in the report and describe the method used, so you can judge the numbers fairly.

## What a useful report includes

- Clicks, add to carts and orders linked to suggestions.
- Revenue linked to those orders, with the method explained.
- Results split by placement: home page, product page, cart, search and email.
- The top and weakest suggested products.
- A view of cart and checkout behavior.
- A before and after comparison where you have earlier data.
- A split of new and returning visitors.
- A split by phone and desktop.
- A list of improvement ideas, ordered by likely value.
- A short note on data gaps and what we could not measure.

## How we produce it

We begin by agreeing which period to report and which tools hold the data: your store analytics, your recommendation tool and, where relevant, your email tool. We check that tracking is working, because a report built on broken tracking misleads.

We then gather the numbers, clean them and compare placements. We write the findings in plain words, add simple charts and finish with next steps. Basic gives you a one page report for one period. Standard adds placement by placement results, product level highlights, a cart and checkout view and a set of ideas. Premium adds a before and after comparison, visitor and device splits, a dashboard link and a walkthrough call.

We report what the data shows. We do not claim that suggestions caused sales unless a test supports it.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Pick a report period that includes a normal stretch of trading.
- Compare placements, not just totals.
- Read linked revenue as a guide, not proof.
- Act on one or two findings at a time.
- Rerun the report after you make changes.

**Avoid:**
- Judging a block after only a few days.
- Comparing a sale week with a quiet week.
- Ignoring phone results when most traffic is on phones.
- Counting every order that touched a suggestion as extra.
- Keeping a weak block because it was expensive to set up.

## Who this is for

This service suits owners who installed a recommendation tool and never checked it, agencies who need a clean summary for a client and teams deciding whether to renew a tool subscription. It also helps stores about to run a test who want a baseline first.

## What we need from you

Tell us which tools and which period to cover. Give us read access to your analytics and recommendation tool as a collaborator or staff user, or send exports. We never need passwords. If your tool has little reporting, say so and we will work from store data.
